description:
A sample which tests two meshes to see if any points of either mesh are inside the other.

To do this, it uses a closest_location lookup to see if it finds a rear-facing normal or not.
documentation:
## Test Inside Mesh Example

### What it does

This demonstrates one way to check whether positions are inside a mesh geometry using a get_closest_location query to test the direction of the normal at the nearest location on the surface of the mesh.

### Inputs and outputs 

This example constructs its own geometry to demonstrate the result. You can substitute your own meshes for the created sphere and cube.

The enclosed point positions are output as a points object, but the points are obscured by the sphere and cube which are also output to show where they are in the scene. Delete the backdrop and the nodes inside it to see the points.

metadata.author: Autodesk
metadata.description:
A sample which tests two meshes to see if any points of either mesh are inside the other.

To do this, it uses a closest_location lookup to see if it finds a rear-facing normal or not.

_notes.text: Feel free to substitute your own meshes here.
Inside this compound we are testing the point normals against the directions of the two points and the point normal.
Make points and set their shape and size
tests to see if the incoming mesh has point normals, provides them if it dosen't

Returns the the array of locations on the input geometry's surface that are closest to each of the input positions.  If `cutoff_distance` is checked, the points will only be returned if they are with the `cutoff_distance`
Samples the positions and normals based on the found locations
Tests the vectors between the points against the point normals.
If the location has been found **and** the point is inside the mesh, then this will return *true* anything else will return *false*
If **any** member of this array is true, it means that the meshes are intersecting.
This compound will return to you all the indicies of the entries in the boolean array that are **true**

_backdrops.title: Get the intersecting points from the position array

_notes.text: If the dot product of the vector between points is going in the same direction as the point normal then it is inside the geometry.  Mathematically, if the dot product is **positive** then the two vectors (`point_normal` is a vector) are going in the same direction hence, the point is inside the second mesh.

# Sine Curve
In this section `sequence_array` is used to create a series of points along the X axis.  These point positions are run through a `sine` compound to get a value between -1 and 1.

The x component is remapped to a 0-1 value and multiplied by an *amplitude* changing the height of the sine curve along the length of the points.

This is added to the origingal point positions and a strand is created.
